_note: Architectural invariants registry (IP-0010). Each entry carries a runnable verifier so CI executes architectural truth every commit. JSON (not YAML) keeps the executor dependency-free. `kind`: grep-absent | loc-budget | test are executed by ops/ci/invariants.py; pyright | script | supply-chain are DELEGATED to the existing CI steps that already run them.

AI-001.name: Runtime Transport Independence
AI-001.rule: the CORE runtime imports no vendor MCP SDK; transports live behind ports

AI-002.name: Single Constitutional Writer
AI-002.rule: the operational loop never authors L3 memory; only the Evolution Layer proposes scars (Stage 17)

AI-003.name: Read-only Evidence Interface
AI-003.rule: the runtime depends on EvidenceSource (read); it never depends on a write facet

AI-004.name: Seal requires adversary PASS
AI-004.rule: no goal seals over a blocking adversarial dissent (FR-3)

AI-005.name: Evidence must be probative
AI-005.rule: evidence with the same result with and without the change cannot seal (vacuous)

AI-007.name: TCB HARD-LOOP
AI-007.rule: kernel/ or constitution/ diffs route to HARD-LOOP

verify.note: needs the merge-base diff; the existing F2 CI step runs it

AI-008.name: No committed keys
AI-008.rule: signing keys never committed; lockfile present

AI-009.name: Constitution read-only
AI-009.rule: no agent write API to Z0; ledger.append is not exposed via MCP

AI-010.name: Port Independence
AI-010.rule: the core depends only on ports (Protocols); adapters/vendors are leaves under runtime/transports/

AI-011.name: Least-Privilege Interface
AI-011.rule: the core depends on the minimal read-only facet of a port (EvidenceSource, not WorkerTransport)
